messages:
maya: :rotating_light: seeing a steady increase in KVCACHE evictions on rack-gpu-07, started ~09:02 UTC. Multiple containers hitting CUDA OOM then restarting.
jonah: on it, logs?
maya: tail from node: `stderr: CudaErrorOutOfMemory: failed to allocate 1.2G` then `kv_alloc: slab split failed, fragmentation > 0.78`
lex: confirmed, paged-attn allocator reporting high free-fragmentation and slow growth in orphaned pages. eviction count +120% in last 10m.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-218432 (sev2) — auto-notified oncall and SRE.
sre-bot: Automated mitigation suggestion: increase kv_evict_threshold to 0.9; enable eager-kv-prune for runtime=on.
maya: trying conservative measures first — plan: 1) route new requests off rack-gpu-07 -> fallback pool, 2) enable eager prune env on the node, 3) scale up dedicated pool by +1 node.
carl: FYI customer-impact: a handful of requests retried; latency spikes for model rmid-7k observed. No P1 customer page yet, but monitoring.
jonah: routing rule applied: `route:set --from rack-gpu-07 --to fallback-lowcpu --duration 30m` confirmed. traffic drop ~95% on that node.
lex: setting env and restart runtime: `kubectl -n redwood set env ds/runtime KVCACHE_EAGER_PRUNE=true --record`
maya: restarting runtime on rack-gpu-07 (graceful drain) — `kubectl drain rack-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
jonah: watch logs: 
```
[09:08:12] runtime: kv_prune: reclaimed 2.3G pages
[09:08:13] runtime: attention_pager: slot_coalesce started
[09:08:15] runtime: CUDA: device 0 free=5.1G total=24G
```
lex: nice, eviction rate dropping back toward baseline. fragmentation metric trending down.
carl: customers: two requests from org-acme-llc got 500s around 09:04 due to container restart, retried successfully. Support notified.
sre-bot: Note: node rack-gpu-07 had kernel-level memory compaction suppressed. Recommend next step if reoccurs: live slab defrag tool (privileged) or move nodes to newer driver.
maya: we should also whitelist model rmid-7k to a lower memory batch config until full postmortem.
jonah: temp config applied: `MODEL_CONFIG_RMID_7K_BATCH=1` on routes serving that model.
lex: open question: why did fragmentated pages not be reclaimed earlier? I see older codepath where kvfree lag can be delayed under heavy batching. Might be scheduler starvation.
maya: can someone run `perf` on the runtime sample? jonah?
jonah: running quick cpu/kv trace now, will post when done.
jonah: trace snippet: `kv_free_worker queued=220 avg_latency_ms=1450` — worker falling behind.
lex: actionable: 1) increase kv_free_worker concurrency to 4, 2) enable eager prune for paged-attn, 3) add a fast-path to reclaim small orphan pages during token flush. I'll open PR for (1)+(3).
maya: rolling change (1) to canary in staging then prod; making a small hotfix to avoid restarts tonight.
carl: customer impact summary for sysops: ~0.02% of requests got 500s, affected 2 orgs, all re-ran. No data leakage. Support message queued.
sre-bot: Reminder: tag incident with label "kv-eviction" and link this thread.
maya: leaving detailed follow-ups for postmortem: timeline, root cause hypothesis (kv_free backlog + driver memory compaction settings), mitigation list (routing, eager-prune env, kv_free concurrency), customer impact.
lex: PR opened: `runtime: bump kv_free_workers, add micro-reclaim path` -> link: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4029
jonah: monitoring: eviction_count back to baseline, cuda oom events stopped.
maya: marking handoff to morning oncall in 1h. if anything flares before then, ping me.
carl: I'll send the customer update draft in #support for review.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-218432 status -> mitigated (investigating).
maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
